newsitem.title: UK: Peel buys stake in Liverpool Airport.
newsitem.headline: Peel buys stake in Liverpool Airport.

text.p: Property group Peel Holdings Plc said on Monday it had bought a 76 percent controlling interest in Liverpool Airport from British Aerospace Plc for an undisclosed sum.
Peel said the acquisition of the airport was a long-term investment in growth opportunities in the Liverpool and Merseyside region.
The purchase was welcomed by deputy prime minister John Prescott who said it represented a major advance for regional development in the north west of England.

"I believe that Peel's new ownership creates a great opportunity for the future of Liverpool Airport as a key element in the provision of airports in the North West," Prescott said at Liverpool Airport.
The group said it hoped to set up a strategic alliance with neighbouring Manchester Airport, previously regarded solely as a competitor.
"The era of confrontation is over," said Robert Hough, deputy chairman of Peel. "What we need is co-operation."
Hough said Liverpool Airport would benefit from advice from its larger international rival on subjects such as terminal and parking facilities expansion, marketing and general airport consultancy.

Peel said Liverpool was the third largest freight and sixth largest mail-handling airport in the UK. It said the airport handled charter traffic and had established scheduled flights to the Isle of Man and Ireland.
It said it would look at ways of building on Liverpool's existing traffic with the possibility of developing flights into Europe.
Hough said the loss-making airport would not contribute to profits in its first year but the purchase was not a short-term investment.

"The airport last year made a loss of around 800,000 pounds but Peel likes long-term challenges," Hough told Reuters. "We will be looking to get good returns in perhaps three, four or five years time."
